Example question(s): Add a note | Make a note about this guest

Example question(s): How many rooms are dirty? (account covers three properties, none active)

Example question(s): Sync rates and restrictions to the channels | Push everything to the OTAs

Phase 1 - what the user sees: Stepper: 1 Scope (rates + restrictions, next 30 days) · 2 Diff (412 changes) · 3 Push · 4 Results: Booking.com ✓, Expedia ✓, Airbnb 3 failed → Retry.
Phase 2 extension (action): Runs the sync and surfaces the log.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: Scope, date range, channels, retry of failures
Notes / reference: new since v0.2: crsBulkSync + OTA push-requests.

Example question(s): Check in Smith with ID capture | Full check-in with passport
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Five steps, one of which deliberately leaves Genie: the ID scan opens the device camera flow and the image never passes through the assistant or the LLM.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Stepper: 1 Room ✓ · 2 Payment guarantee ✓ · 3 ID scan (opens scanner - image stays on device) · 4 Registration card · 5 Confirm & encode key.
RBAC check (Module → Feature → Permissio: Front Desk → Manage Reservation → UPDATE + Documentation Management → Edit Document → UPDATE
Phase 2 extension (action): Orchestrates the steps; the scan stays outside the LLM path by design.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: Room, payment, ID type, signature capture
Phase 2 audit log fields: actor, reservation id, document ids, key encoded
Notes / reference: PII boundary made visible as a step, per the doc's data-classification rules.

Example question(s): Set up today's housekeeping | Plan the floor
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Four steps: pull the dirty and due-out list, propose a split across the housekeepers on shift, adjust, then publish and notify.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Stepper: 1 17 rooms (11 dirty, 6 due-out) · 2 Proposed split across Maria, Ana, Jose · 3 Adjust · 4 Publish & notify.
Phase 2 extension (action): Publishes the assignments and notifies the team.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: Who is on shift, split shape, notify

Example question(s): Reconcile yesterday's cash | Daily collection check
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Four steps: pull collections by payment type, compare against the shift reports, flag the variance, then record the explanation against the day.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Stepper: 1 Collections by type · 2 Shift reports · 3 Variance −$40 flagged · 4 Record the explanation.
RBAC check (Module → Feature → Permissio: Reports → Daily Collection by Payment Type → READ + Reports → Daily Shift Report → READ
Phase 2 extension (action): Records the reconciliation note against the business date.
Phase 2 audit log fields: actor, business date, variance, note id
Notes / reference: new since v0.2: daily-collection and daily-collection-by-payment-type reports.

Example question(s): Add my second property | Set up the new hotel
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Six steps mirroring the create-property wizard, with Genie carrying answers between steps rather than making the owner re-enter them.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Stepper: 1 Basics · 2 Room types & rooms · 3 Rate types · 4 Taxes · 5 Users & roles · 6 Go live checklist.
Phase 2 extension (action): Drives the wizard; each step still writes through the module's own API.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: Every wizard slot, carried between steps
Notes / reference: new since v0.2: create-property-steps components. The longest stepper in the product.

Example question(s): Mark 201 clean | 201 is done
Phase 1 - how it is handled: The reversible write. Genie applies it immediately after a soft confirm and holds an undo window; the front desk sees the change in real time.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Room 201 · vacant dirty → vacant clean' with 'Undo (8s)' and 'Front desk notified'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Applies the status and holds the undo window.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: Room if ambiguous; inspected vs clean
Notes / reference: the archetype: fast, reversible, no interruption.

Example question(s): The AC in 305 is broken - log it | Report a maintenance issue
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Genie creates the task with the location and priority it inferred, shows both, and lets the reporter correct them inside the undo window instead of asking first.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Service request #8842 created · Room 305 · AC · High · routed to Maintenance' with 'Undo' and 'Change priority'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Creates and routes the task.
Phase 2 audit log fields: actor, task id, type, room, priority
Notes / reference: correcting after the fact beats interrogating before it, for a reversible create.

Example question(s): Assign floor 3 to Maria
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Assignment lands immediately with an undo, because the cost of a wrong assignment is a conversation, not money.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Floor 3 · 11 rooms assigned to Maria for today' with 'Undo (8s)' and 'Maria notified'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Writes the assignment and notifies.

Example question(s): Add a shift note: 240 wants a late checkout, confirm with the morning desk
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Genie writes the note verbatim, attributed and timestamped, and keeps the undo window because a mistyped note is read by the next shift.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Shift note added · Priya · 22:04' with the text shown back and 'Undo'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Creates the note.

Example question(s): Note on 4471: guest asked for a high floor
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Reservation-scoped note, applied at once. The card states where the note lives so it is not confused with a profile note that follows the guest.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Note added to #4471 (this stay only)' with 'Undo' and 'Add to the guest profile instead'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Writes the note to the reservation.

Example question(s): Flag Rodriguez as VIP | Mark her as a VIP guest
Phase 1 - how it is handled: One-tap flag with an undo, and the card names the consequence: every department sees it from now on.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Maria Rodriguez flagged VIP · visible to front desk, housekeeping and F&B' with 'Undo'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Sets the flag on the profile.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: VIP tier if the property uses tiers

Example question(s): Add a DNR flag for that guest | Do not rent to them again
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Reversible but consequential: the card requires a reason from the property's DNR reason list and shows who will see it.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: DNR set · reason: damage to room · visible on every future booking attempt' with 'Undo (8s)'.
RBAC check (Module → Feature → Permissio: Guest → Guest Profile → UPDATE + Property Configuration → DNR Reasons → READ
Phase 2 extension (action): Sets the flag with its reason code.
Notes / reference: new since v0.2: dnr-reasons configuration. A reason code turns a grudge into a record.

Example question(s): Her phone number is wrong - it's 555 0142
Phase 1 - how it is handled: A single-field correction applies at once, with the old value shown so the undo is meaningful and the audit trail readable.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Phone updated · 555 0198 → 555 0142' with 'Undo' and the audit note.
Phase 2 extension (action): Writes the field.

Example question(s): Add a folio notice about the pool closure
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Notices print on guest documents, so the card previews exactly where it will appear before the undo window closes.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Folio notice added · appears on folios and registration cards from today' with a preview line and 'Undo'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Creates the notice.
Notes / reference: new since v0.2: folioNotices API.

Example question(s): Mark those six rooms Vacant | 204, 206, 210, 214, 218, 220 are Vacant
Phase 1 - how it is handled: A bulk reversible write: one undo reverts all six, and the card lists them so a mis-heard room number is visible.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: 6 rooms → inspected: 204, 206, 210, 214, 218, 220' with 'Undo all (8s)'.
RBAC check (Module → Feature → Permissio: Housekeeping Management → Change Room Status in Bulk → UPDATE
Phase 2 extension (action): Applies the bulk status change.

Example question(s): Mark that task resolved | The 305 request is done
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Resolution stamps a time and an actor. The undo exists because 'done' is sometimes said about the wrong task.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Task #8842 resolved · 09:14 · by Sai' with 'Undo' and 'Reopen'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Resolves the task with its timestamp.
Notes / reference: RESOLVE is a real permission verb in the matrix, not a synonym for UPDATE.

Example question(s): Email me the daily summary every morning | Send the owner a weekly digest
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Scheduling is reversible, so it applies at once with the schedule stated in words rather than cron terms, and the undo cancels the whole schedule.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Daily summary · 07:00 · to you and owner@… · starting tomorrow' with 'Undo' and 'Change time'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Creates the schedule.

Example question(s): I've dealt with that action item | Acknowledge the expiring card auth
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Acknowledgement is not resolution. The card is explicit that the underlying item still exists, and the undo puts it back on the list.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Acknowledged · hidden from your list until tomorrow. The card authorisation still expires at 18:00.' with 'Undo'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Marks the item acknowledged for this user.
Notes / reference: the copy has to prevent 'acknowledged' being read as 'fixed'.

Example question(s): Resend the confirmation to Smith
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Sending is irreversible once it leaves, so the undo window is a hold-and-send: Genie queues for 8 seconds before dispatch and says so.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Confirmation queued for maria@… · sending in 8s' with 'Undo' - then 'Sent 14:03' once the window closes.
RBAC check (Module → Feature → Permissio: Reservation → Reservation → UPDATE + Settings → Email → READ
Phase 2 extension (action): Holds, then sends, and logs the send against the reservation.
Phase 2 audit log fields: actor, reservation id, template, recipient, sent at
Notes / reference: an undo on an outbound email must be a delay, not a promise to unsend.

Example question(s): How much did we take on cards yesterday? | Card totals by type for the month
Phase 1 - how it is handled: daily-credit-card-summary report for the business date, grouped by card type. Genie returns totals and counts only - never a card number, at any role.

Phase 1 - how it is handled: daily-collection-by-payment-type for the business date; deterministic totals per method with the shift breakdown available behind the link.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Card: Cash $1,240 · Card $4,318 · Direct bill $860 · total $6,418 + 'Open Daily Collection by Payment Type'.

Example question(s): What reports do we have? | Is there a report for deposits?
Phase 1 - how it is handled: reportCatalog API filtered by the user's permissions, so the list only names reports the user can actually open.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: List of matching reports with one line each + 'Open Reports'. Reports the role can't read are not listed at all.

Example question(s): Who changed this reservation and when? | Show me the history of 4471
Phase 1 - how it is handled: The entity-trail audit view for one record: every change, actor, timestamp and old → new value, in order.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Timeline: created 12 Jun (OTA) · rate changed 18 Jun (Sai) · room assigned 25 Jun (Priya) · note added 25 Jun + 'Open the full trail'.

Example question(s): Why was I logged out? | It signed me out mid-sentence
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Genie recognises the post-logout question and explains the inactivity policy and the device limit, without asking the user to re-describe what happened.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Notice: 'You were signed out after 30 minutes of inactivity. Your last question was kept.' + 'Sign in again'.

Example question(s): It says I've hit the device limit | Why can't I sign in on this iPad?
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Explains the max-device policy and names the action the user has to take, without exposing which other devices are signed in.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Notice: 'Your account is signed in on the maximum number of devices. Sign out of one, or ask an Admin to release a session.' + 'Open Device Configuration'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Release a device session after confirm.

Example question(s): Did the OTA push go through? | Any failed channel pushes?
Phase 1 - how it is handled: ota push-requests + file-mapping status for the last run, with failures separated from successes and a retry offered per failure.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: List: Booking.com ✓ 09:02 · Expedia ✓ 09:02 · Airbnb 3 failed 09:03 + 'Open Push Requests'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Retry the failed pushes.

Example question(s): Which rate types are inactive? | Is the Summer Promo still live?
Phase 1 - how it is handled: rate-type list with activation and deactivation windows resolved against the business date.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: List: BAR active · Corporate active · Summer Promo inactive since 1 Sep · Winter Promo starts 1 Nov + 'Open Rate Type'.
RBAC check (Module → Feature → Permissio: Rates and Availability → Rate Type → READ
Phase 2 extension (action): Activate or deactivate after a preview.

Example question(s): Save this as my default view | What views do I have?
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Reads the user's saved views and offers them as navigation targets; Phase 1 links, it does not create.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: List of saved views with 'Open' per row + 'Manage views'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Creates or updates a saved view.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: View name, which filters to keep

Example question(s): How do I invite a new front-desk user? | Add Priya to the team
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Guide from the help corpus plus a deep link to the invite screen with the role preselected. Phase 1 never sends an invite - an invite grants access.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Guide + citation, then 'Open Users → Invite' with Desk Staff preselected.
Phase 2 extension (action): Sends the invite after a preview.

Example question(s): Download the folio for Smith | Download the registration form for room 204 | Print the detailed folio for booking #4471
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Resolve the reservation (name, room, or confirmation number) and infer the document type from the message (folio, detailed, other charges, registration, payment receipt, group status report). Document generation is non-mutating, so Phase 1 returns the existing Print Folio endpoint directly as a download.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Reservation resolved → 'Here's your download' card with the PDF + 'Open reservation'.
Phase 2 extension (action): Email this document instead of downloading it (see email_folio).
Notes / reference: Reuses the same endpoint and RBAC tier as the Print Folio menu in the UI.

Example question(s): Email the folio for Smith | Email the registration form for room 204 to the guest
Phase 1 - how it is handled: Resolve the reservation and document type exactly like download_folio, then resolve the recipient (the reservation POC unless the user names another address). Returns a confirm card naming the recipient before sending anything. Only on an explicit 'yes/send it' reply does Genie call the existing Email Folio endpoint with the signed-in user's token; the server's own RBAC and validation are the real gate.
Phase 1 - what the user sees: Confirm card ('Email the folio for Smith to the POC on file — send it?') → on Yes, an 'Email sent' card; on No or silence, nothing is sent.
Phase 2 extension (action): Batch-email a document to every in-house guest; schedule recurring folio emails.
Phase 2 clarifications / multi-step: Recipient email if the POC is missing or the user wants a different address
Phase 2 audit log fields: actor, reservation id, docType, recipient (redacted), result
Notes / reference: First Genie-initiated write: requires an explicit confirm turn, calls POST /folio/{id}/email once, and is logged the same way every tool call already is (internal/store ToolExecution).
